package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2, 5)
	s[0], s[1] = 1, 2
	v := s[:2:2]
	v = append(v, 9)
	fmt.Println(s[1])
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(v[2])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 2)
	s = append(s, 3)
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	s := make([]int, 3)
	s = append(s, 4)
	fmt.Println(len(s))
	fmt.Println(cap(s))
}
What is the capacity of t := s[i:j:k]?
options: k - i. The third index clips cap, not len
cap(s) - i, same as s[i:j]
j - i
k

questions.text: Why take s[:n:n] before append?
options: So that len becomes n*2
So cap becomes n and append cannot overwrite the rest of the original array
It forbids append
To copy the elements into a new array at once

questions.text: What does append into s[:i] do when unused cap remains?
options: It always allocates a new array
It writes only past the original len; s[i:] is untouched
It writes into the same array and overwrites s[i], s[i+1], …
It panics if i < cap

questions.text: How does copy behave on overlapping slices of one array?
options: The result is undefined
It always panics
Only the non-overlapping part is copied
The copy is correct, like memmove: overlap does not scramble the data

questions.text: Where does append(s, s...) take the elements to append from?
options: From a snapshot of the original s before growth: the old length is appended
From s after it grew, so the duplication is different
Only the first element of s
The compiler rejects it

questions.text: Does slices.Equal treat nil and empty []int{} as equal?
options: No, only == treats them that way
Yes: it compares elements, and both are empty
Yes only if both also have cap 0
It panics

questions.text: What does s[:0] keep?
options: Only the pointer; cap becomes 0
Nothing: it is a new nil
The same array and the old cap, length 0 — the buffer can be reused
The length, but not cap

questions.text: What can a function do to a slice argument without returning a new header?
options: Grow the caller’s variable len
Replace the caller’s cap
Make the caller’s variable nil
Write elements of the shared array; the caller’s own len/cap do not change

questions.text: What does slices.Clip(s) do?
options: It returns s[:len(s):len(s)] — cap becomes equal to len
It clears the slice
It always copies elements into a new array
It trims len down to cap

questions.text: How does slices.Clone(s) differ from t := s[:]?
options: Not at all: both share the array
Clone copies elements into a new array; s[:] is only a new header
Clone zeros the original s
s[:] copies; Clone does not

questions.text: Why does writing v.N in for _, v := range []T not change the slice?
options: range forbids writing to v
T is always immutable
v is a copy of the element, not the slot in the array
range walks a one-shot copy of the whole slice

questions.text: What does slices.Grow(s, n) do to len?
options: It increases len by n
It sets len to n
It zeros len
It leaves len unchanged; if needed it grows cap so n appends need no new array

questions.text: What does slices.Delete(s, i, j) do to the array tail past the new len (Go 1.21+)?
options: It zeros the evicted elements so they do not keep references alive
It leaves the old values in the tail, like append(s[:i], s[j:]...)
It always allocates a new array
It sets cap to 0

questions.text: How large may k be in s[i:j:k]?
options: k ≤ len(s)
k ≤ cap(s). Otherwise it panics
k is unbounded
k ≤ j

questions.text: When must append on a subslice take a new array, looking only at that subslice’s cap?
options: When the new len is ≤ cap of the original s, even if the subslice cap is exhausted
Never: a subslice always writes into the original array
When the subslice’s new length is greater than its own cap
Only if the subslice was nil

questions.text: Why does copy into a dst with len 0 copy nothing even if cap(dst) > 0?
options: copy looks at cap(dst)
It is a compile error
copy requires dst to be nil
copy transfers min(len(dst), len(src)); if len(dst)=0 that is 0

questions.text: s[i:j:j] has capacity equal to its length.
append into s[:i] with spare cap never overwrites s[i].
copy on overlapping slices of one array is defined and safe.
slices.Equal treats nil and empty []int as equal.
s[:0] sets capacity to 0.
A function can change the caller’s s[0] without returning a slice.
A function can grow the caller’s slice len without returning append’s result.
slices.Clip makes cap equal to len.
In for _, v := range []struct{...}, writing v changes the slice element.
The third index in s[i:j:k] cannot be greater than cap(s).
append(s, s...) always keeps the same backing array.
slices.Clone(s) shares s’s array.
After Clip, appending one element no longer fits the old cap and takes a new array.
slices.Insert can increase a slice’s length.
copy into a slice with len 0 copies cap(dst) elements when cap > 0.
s[:k] panics when k > cap(s).
What is the capacity of s[i:j:k]?
Why write s[:n:n] before append?
questions.answer: To clip cap to n so append cannot overwrite the rest of the original array.

questions.text: What happens to s[i] if you append into s[:i] while spare cap remains?
questions.answer: The new element is written at s[i] of the same array.

questions.text: Is copy safe when dst and src overlap?
questions.answer: Yes. It behaves like memmove; the data is not scrambled.

questions.text: How many elements does append(s, s...) add?
questions.answer: As many as len(s) was before the call.

questions.text: What does slices.Clip do?
questions.answer: It returns a slice with cap = len, same array up to that new bound.

questions.text: Besides length 0, what does s[:0] keep?
questions.answer: The pointer and the old capacity — the buffer can be filled again.

questions.text: Are nil and []int{} equal for slices.Equal?
questions.answer: Yes. It compares elements; both are empty.

questions.text: Why does for _, v := range not change []T?
questions.answer: v is a copy of the element.

questions.text: Does slices.Clone copy the backing array?
questions.answer: Yes. A new array with the same elements.

questions.text: Does append inside a function change the caller’s argument len?
questions.answer: No, unless the result is returned and assigned outside.

questions.text: Does slices.Grow change length?
questions.answer: No. Only cap grows if needed.

questions.text: What does slices.Delete do to the tail past the new len?
What bounds the third index k in s[i:j:k]?
questions.answer: k is at most cap(s), otherwise panic.

questions.text: Why does copy into a len-0 dst copy nothing?
questions.answer: The count is min(len(dst), len(src)), and len(dst) is 0.

questions.text: What happens for s[:k] if k > cap(s)?
questions.answer: panic: slice bounds out of range.
